sections.h2: What should I know about Shelbyville before selling a house there?
sections.html:
Shelbyville is the seat of Bedford County, laid out in 1810 and incorporated in 1819, on a limestone bluff of the Highland Rim where the Duck River curls around the south and east sides of town. It covers about 18.4 square miles, and US 231 meets US 41A in town. Locals call it the Pencil City, and the Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration, which began in 1939, fills the 11 days before Labor Day every year.

The Census Bureau estimates 26,146 residents as of July 1, 2025, a gain of 11.1% since the 2020 census base, and a long way up from the 20,335 counted in 2010. Manufacturing and distribution anchor the local economy, with Musgrave Pencil, a Tyson facility, a Walmart distribution center and several trucking firms among the employers Wikipedia names. Those jobs, plus a county seat's courts and offices, shape who buys here.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers tell a Shelbyville seller?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the typical owner-occupied house in Shelbyville is valued at $244,000, the lowest figure among these four Tennessee cities, and only 50.7% of occupied homes have their owner living in them. A renter pays a median $1,056. The 9,089 households average 2.64 people, and 28.4% of residents are under 18, so family houses with several bedrooms are a core product.

  • Median household income: $55,073 in 2024 dollars
  • Residents below the poverty line: 20.7%
  • College graduates among adults 25 and older: 13.1%
  • Mean commute: 27.2 minutes
  • Foreign-born residents: 15.3%, and 25.6% of people age 5 and over speak another language at home

With half the housing rented, investor-owned houses and small rental properties turn over regularly. Details are on Census QuickFacts for Shelbyville.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 reappraisal change Bedford County tax rates?
sections.html:
On June 30, 2026 the county commission approved $198 million in budgets and held the property tax at the state's certified rate. Bedford County was in a reappraisal year, and most owners received higher appraisals. The old rate of $2.3252 for every $100 assessed dropped to the certified $1.5083, so the average owner should see little change in the bill unless a value rose faster than the county average.

Residential parcels are assessed at one quarter of appraised value, so the $244,000 Census median becomes $61,000 on the roll and about $920 of county tax before any city levy. Source: the county's budget announcement.

sections.h2: Does a lower county rate always mean a lower tax bill?
sections.html:
Not automatically. The state sets a certified rate after a reappraisal so the county collects about the same total from existing property, and the county says any rate above that figure counts as a tax increase for most owners. A bill still moves when your own value rose faster or slower than the county average, or when you added improvements.

Assessed value is only a share of appraised value, which for a house is 25 percent. If you are weighing offers, ask the Assessor of Property which value is on your parcel record and whether a recent addition, like a garage or a deck, has been picked up.

sections.h2: Does Shelbyville have its own property tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. The city takes payment for its levy separately from the county. Pay online or by phone through a third-party processor that adds a fee, by mail to the City of Shelbyville, P.O. Box 185, Shelbyville, TN 37162, or in person at City Hall, 201 North Spring Street on the Public Square. Include the top stub and write the receipt number on a mailed check.

Ask the city for the current-year city rate, since the county announcement covers only the county portion. Under the Comptroller's calendar, the new year's bill comes due on the first Monday of October, while the prior year's bill stays interest-free through February 28. Because two jurisdictions bill separately, a seller should ask the title company to pull both statements before closing.

sections.h2: Is there tax relief for older or disabled owners in Bedford County?
sections.html:
Bedford County's freeze cap on income is $43,780 for 2026 on the Comptroller's list, compared with the statewide floor of $38,470. Filing closes 35 days after the delinquency date, in April. Other relief programs exist for disabled veterans and for elderly or disabled owners with low income.

The freeze holds the bill at what it was in the first approved year, so mention it to the buyer's side if your house carries one. On a larger lot, ask the assessor about greenbelt classification, which has a March 15 application deadline.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect a Shelbyville sale?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department, at (931) 488-4230, requires a permit to build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or demolish a structure, and also for pools, decks, arbors and storage buildings. Permits and applications now run only through the city's OpenGov portal, and some residential, fence, sign, accessory structure and driveway applications are online only. The department enforces the 2018 International Codes, and simple permits can be issued the same day.

If a buyer wants a different zoning, the process runs through the Planning Department, a pre-planning meeting, the Planning Commission and two City Council readings, and the ordinance takes effect 15 days after the public hearing. A sale usually does not need a rezoning, but confirm the current zone before you promise a buyer a use such as a duplex or a home business.

  • Call before you start any repair that changes structure or systems.
  • Keep permit finals with your closing documents.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded at the Bedford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Register records documents that give public notice of ownership, liens and contracts, and reports the state's conveyance and mortgage taxes to the Department of Revenue each month. The office has an online fee calculator for any filing, and a free fraud alert service that notifies you of transfers recorded under your name. State law puts 37 cents on every $100 of sale price, plus 11.5 cents per $100 of mortgage debt beyond the first $2,000.

On the $244,000 Census median, the 37-cent levy comes to $902.80. A title company normally files the deed, and the sale contract names which side pays.

sections.h2: What does Shelbyville's setting mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Shelbyville averages about 59.4 inches of precipitation across roughly 128 days a year, and snow totals only about an inch. Summer highs average near 89 degrees in July, with a recorded top of 108. With that much moisture, expect an inspector to look hard at roofs, crawl spaces and drainage.

Bedford County School District runs the public schools, and Shelbyville Central High School is the local high school. The district sets attendance zones, so confirm a specific address with the district.

sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Shelbyville?
sections.html:
A standard listing gets the most eyes on the house. A cash buyer who takes it with tenants in place or repairs undone can close as fast as title work allows.

Weigh a cash figure against what a listing would leave after commission, repairs and holding costs. Get the offer in writing, clear the county and city tax statements, and let a title company record the deed.

faqs.q: What is the Bedford County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: On June 30, 2026 the commission adopted the state's certified rate of $1.5083, which replaces last year's $2.3252. The city bills its own tax separately.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Shelbyville city property tax?
faqs.a: At City Hall, 201 North Spring Street, by mail to P.O. Box 185, online, or by phone at 1-866-414-2699. Online and phone payments carry a third-party fee.

faqs.q: Can I get a permit for a fence or accessory building in Shelbyville?
faqs.a: Yes, through the city's OpenGov portal. Fence, accessory structure, sign and driveway applications are online only. Call (931) 488-4230 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Shelbyville sale?
faqs.a: The state takes 37 cents per $100 of price, so a $244,000 sale carries $902.80 at recording. Your contract says who pays it.

faqs.q: What is the freeze income limit for Bedford County?
faqs.a: $43,780 for tax year 2026, according to the Comptroller. Applicants must be 65 or older and meet the program's ownership and residence rules.
